prompts.task: Treat ./service as the project root. The otel-audit report for this fixture is provided at ./service/otel-audit.json (the harness strips committed .observe/ inputs, so it is shipped here instead). FIRST create ./service/.observe/ and copy ./service/otel-audit.json to ./service/.observe/otel-audit.json. For this offline audit-only fixture, explicitly accept exactly http.server.request.duration and http.server.active_requests as source-only detector inputs; no other audit metric is accepted and source presence must not be described as emitted-datapoint proof. THEN generate detector Terraform for ./service so every output is written under ./service/.observe/ and ./service/.observe/terraform/. Generate one signalfx_detector resource per supported classification intent, applying Route-Level De-duplication so checkout.payment.errors is merged into the http.server.request.duration route group rather than getting its own resource, plus variables.tf, terraform.tfvars.example, the .observe/detectors.md report, and the .observe/splunk-configure-verify.md verification file. Run the skill's Python configure-output validator in audit-only detector mode with the canonical audit JSON and those two exact --allow-source-only-metric values, without supplying partial downstream overlay inputs. Keep the configure result Partial because emitted datapoints and authenticated SignalFlow compilation remain unproven, even if the local structural validator passes. Do not call any network and do not run terraform.

judge_inputs: Inspect ./service/.observe for the resulting files when present, especially ./service/.observe/terraform/detectors.tf, ./service/.observe/terraform/variables.tf, ./service/.observe/detectors.md, and ./service/.observe/splunk-configure-verify.md.
Read ./last_message.md for the agent final response.
rubric: Reads the canonical audit at .observe/otel-audit.json and treats only the explicitly accepted source-only http.server.request.duration and http.server.active_requests metrics as detector inputs. It does not generate detectors from http.server.request.size, http.server.response.size, checkout.orders.processed, or checkout.payment.errors, and never describes source presence as emitted-datapoint proof.

Classifies the accepted checkout metrics into latency (http.server.request.duration → P99 threshold) and at least one of throughput or saturation (http.server.request.duration count or http.server.active_requests).

Applies Route-Level De-duplication from detector-classification.md: since the audit states http.server.request.duration already carries an error.type attribute for POST /payment covering the same 502 outcome checkout.payment.errors counts, the error detector reads http.server.request.duration filtered on error.type rather than treating checkout.payment.errors as an independently classified metric. checkout.payment.errors may still appear in detectors.md as a metric merged into that route group, but must not get its own detector resource whose only differentiator from the latency detector is the metric name.

Writes signalfx_detector resources to .observe/terraform/detectors.tf: each resource has a name, program_text with a valid SignalFlow expression referencing the correct metric and a filter('service.name', '${var.service_name}') constraint, and at least one rule block with a severity (Critical/Major/Minor/Warning). Either a detect(when(...)) expression or an against_recent(...) / alerts_and_clears(...) baseline pattern is acceptable. A detector reading http.server.request.duration for the merged error case must add both a route filter (e.g. filter('http.route', '/payment')) and a failing-outcome filter (e.g. filter('error.type', '*')), so it stays scoped to the /payment route the counter was merged from and is distinguishable from the latency detector on the same metric -- a detector filtered only by service.name and error.type aggregates failures across every route and does not satisfy this criterion.

Each detector program_text uses the data('<metric>', filter=filter('service.name', ...)).<agg>().publish() pattern with either a detect(when(... > threshold)) tail or an against_recent / baseline alerting tail appropriate for the detector category — a plain publish() without any detection logic is not acceptable, but the skill has latitude to choose threshold vs. baseline-comparison style.

Writes variables.tf with realm, api_token marked sensitive = true, and service_name, plus at least one tunable variable per detector (either a static threshold variable like latency_threshold_s, error_rate_threshold, throughput_min_threshold OR a baseline parameter like fire_lasting_duration, clear_lasting_duration), and a terraform.tfvars.example; never hard-codes a real token or a literal service name in program_text.

Runs validate_configure_output.py in audit-only detector mode with .observe/otel-audit.json and exact --allow-source-only-metric exceptions for http.server.request.duration and http.server.active_requests, supplies no partial selection/instrumentation/verification overlay set, and records the local validator outcome separately from telemetry proof.

Writes .observe/detectors.md summarising the classified detectors, their metrics, severities, rationale, skipped metrics, and source-only limitations. It reports the configure result as Partial because emitted datapoints and authenticated SignalFlow compilation were not proven, then hands off to terraform apply or $splunk-detector-publish without performing any network call or Terraform CLI command.

Writes .observe/splunk-configure-verify.md listing each generated detector with at least its resource label (or name), the metric it monitors, its severity, the source-only authorization, and the remaining emitted-data and remote-compilation gaps; full detect condition text is desirable but not required for this criterion to pass.
